newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower, specs continue to liquidate.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower, specs continue to liquidate.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures fell to fresh eight-week lows on Wednesday, as speculators continued to liquidate long positions amid bearish technicals and abundent nearby supplies, dealers said.
"There's plentiful supply, disappointed longs liquidating and no bullish news," said Refco analyst Ann Prendergast. "The path of least resistance is lower."
Benchmark July futures ended $14 a tonne lower, at $1,400, after ranging from $1,410 to $1,392. Spot May also fell $14, to $1,394, while the back months closed $12 lower to $6 higher.
After plummeting some $40 on Tuesday, traders said continued speculative liquidation pushed the market into negative territory at the outset.
News that broker GNI cut its 1996/97 world cocoa deficit estimate to 33,000 tonnes from its earlier forecast of 180,000 tonnes set a bearish tone, traders said.

GNI said its reduced deficit projection was due to an increased production estimate for top-grower Ivory Coast. They put total 1996/97 Ivorian output at 1.15 million tonnes, including a 160,000-tonne mid-crop.

The July contract managed to hold above key psychological support at $1,400 for much of the day, but an afternoon sell-off pushed prices to session lows. Traders said scale-down industry buying and some bottom-picking by speculators helped to trim losses by the close.
On the charts, traders pegged nearby July support at $1,385-$1.380, with a solid downside target noted at $1,365. Resistance was seen near yesterday's close at $1,414, followed by $1,420.
Volume was moderate, at an estimated 7,072 lots.
